claims.claim_ar: قُلْ: فعل أمر موجّه مخاطبًا، صيغة أمر من الفعل الثلاثي المجرد (الجذر: ق-و-ل).
claims.claim_en: قُلْ is an imperative (command) from the triliteral root ق-و-ل (to say/recite); a direct vocative/imperative verb form.

claims.claim_ar: حَرَّمَ: وزن فعلي فَعَّلَ (صيغة تفعل/تشديد) من الجذر ح-ر-م، دالّة على التحريم كفعل مبالَغ/مؤثّر.
claims.claim_en: The verb حَرَّمَ follows the fa''ala (فَعَّلَ) pattern — an intensive/causative template from root ح-ر-م — denoting the act of forbidding/declaring forbidden.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source quote is the plural past form 'حَرَّمُوا' while the ayah contains the singular past 'حَرَّمَ'; check number/voice alignment between example and the ayah.

claims.claim_ar: تَقْتُلُوا (في الآية: لَا تَقْتُلُوا): صيغة مضارع مجزوم تُستعمل هنا في سياق النهي/التحريم، بينما الشرح يستشهد بصيغة الماضي 'قَتَلُوا' كخبر عن فعل وقع — فرق الزمان/الصيغة قد يغيّر نبرة الترجمة (النهي التحريمي مقابل تقرير فعل ماضٍ).
claims.claim_en: The ayah uses the present jussive 'تَقْتُلُوا' in a prohibitive sense ('do not kill'), whereas the commentary cites the past 'قَتَلُوا' (they killed). This aspect/tense shift can create a translation nuance (prohibitive present vs reported past action).
claims.needs_review_reason: Source quotation is past plural 'قَتَلُوا' while the ayah has present jussive 'تَقْتُلُوا'; confirm intended morphological/semantic point in context.

claims.claim_ar: نَرْزُقُكُمْ: فعل مضارع من الجذر ر-ز-ق، دال على الإعطاء/المنّ بالرزق؛ في الشرح وردت صيغة الماضي 'رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ' لتوضيح أن الرزق من عند الله.
claims.claim_en: نَرْزُقُكُمْ is the imperfect verb from root ر-ز-ق meaning 'to provide/provide sustenance'; the commentary cites 'رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ' (past) to indicate that provision comes from God.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source quote uses a past form ('رَزَقَهُمُ') while the ayah uses a present imperfect ('نَرْزُقُكُمْ'); root meaning is stable but aspect/form difference noted.

warnings: Source material are i'rab/commentary chunks that include forms and examples not always in the exact same tense/number as the ayah. Several claims are anchored to chunk substrings whose verbal form (tense/number) differs from the ayah's form; these differences are noted in needs_review_reason for each claim.
Only claims with an exact substring match in the provided source chunks were extracted. Many ayah words did not have an exact match in the chunks, so no morphological claim was made for them.
